doc.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: First seeing Goodman, and varying tunes through the night
summary: Sol saw Goodman at the stage door in 1937 and explains how he keeps repeated songs fresh.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You couldn’t believe how tall he was?
Yeah he didn’t seem like a tall person.

He was six foot two, oh yeah. And I still love to play. I never get bored playing. If I have to play a song four or five times a night it doesn’t bother me, I’ll play it at different tempos or I’ll play it in a different key. I know how to get around little things like that. If I have to play a song like “As Time Goes By,” I can play it like —[Sol plays] — or if I have to play it again I’ll play it — [Sol plays] — you know to give it a little twist. Like with Tony Bennett “San Francisco,” he has to sing that every show for the past 50 years. So imagine Benny Goodman playing “Don’t Be That Way” and “Sing Sing Sing,” it was unbelievable.
